body.x: BizCrush, Inc. (CEO Taemin Kwak) participated on Monday, the 27th, in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ hosted for domestic companies and startups by AVING News’ ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ at the MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

Running for four days from July 27 to 30, this ‘Global Media Meetup’ focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to report to global media in advance on the products and technologies of companies participating in global exhibitions, including CES 2027, and to expand business opportunities. BizCrush CEO Taemin Kwak delivered the presentation on this day.

Backed by Google for Startups and operating as a US Delaware C-Corp with a Korean entity, BizCrush is an AI technology pioneer specializing in real-time, multilingual speech recognition, translation, and automated meeting record generation. Founded by CEO Taemin Kwak (holding more than 9 registered patents), who developed production systems in STT (speech-to-text) and natural language processing fields for over 8 years, and CTO Ethan Kim (Jaeyeop Kim), a Google open-source contributor, the company was established in 2025 on a global-market premise from the outset. Ahead of its official commercial Enterprise release, BizCrush is actively building its global presence by exhibiting at CES 2027 in Las Vegas and entering its proprietary technology into the CES 2027 Innovation Awards in AI Software & Mobile Apps and Accessibility.

BizCrush assists communication with real-time subtitles and translation while meetings progress, connecting conversations to summaries, follow-up tasks, and meeting minutes after meetings end. Its voice pipeline automatically recognizes 60 languages without separate configurations and processes conversations where languages switch within a single sentence. It delivers real-time performance across iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows, serving subtitles within 0.4 to 0.5 seconds of the utterance, translations in about 2.5 seconds, and listener-specific AI voice dubbing within 5 seconds.

Its core competitiveness lies in ‘accuracy in actual operating environments.’ In quiet lab environments, recognition error rates for major services appear to be similar, at around 4–6 percent. Still, in real environments with background noise, such as cafes or event venues, error rates soar. BizCrush approaches this issue with a patent-pending on-device speech enhancement engine that filters out ambient noise and refines speech inside user devices before audio reaches recognition engines. Furthermore, it operates a public benchmark platform that publishes measurement methodologies, raw audio data, and competitors’ outputs. As of July 2026, its Character Error Rate (CER) in high-noise environments with loud background sounds reached the 41 percent range—lower than competing services at 46 to 60 percent—and its overall average error rate was 22.8 percent, the lowest among services listed on the benchmark.

body.x: Products include subscription apps for individuals and teams ($7.99 to $29.99/month) and on-site solutions for conferences and exhibitions. The on-site solution broadcasts stage utterances as real-time translated subtitles on large screens, allowing attendees to receive subtitles in their own languages on their mobile devices by simply scanning a QR code without installing an app or signing up. It also supports interpretation and recording in 1-on-1 consultation booths. Adding an ‘adaptive glossary’ to this, users register terminology in advance or upload PDFs to configure initial dictionaries, and recognition accuracy steadily rises as the system learns user names, technical terminology, and abbreviations over repeated meetings. Built with privacy in mind by the architecture, it also offers a “Privacy Mode” where live scripts stream without saving audio recordings, while allowing secure export directly to a client’s private storage or Notion.

Track records accumulate as well. BizCrush operated real-time transcription and translation solutions across 12 events and sites in Korea and the US in 2026 alone. In the US, it signed an MOU with the Korean Education Center in Seattle to support the 2026 PNW Korean Speaking Contest and conducted a pilot with Lynnwood, Washington. Participating as an official technology partner in ‘Korean Night with Carmen’ co-hosted by the Consulate General of the Republic of Korea in Seattle and Seattle Opera, it operated American events such as Georgia KAGC 2026 and Auburn University’s AUAI AI Summit in Alabama. In Korea, it handled real-time subtitles and translations for major conferences including Skill-Up Festa 2026, WIS 2026, and Changbal Dev Conference. In the corporate sector, domestic call centers adopted it as an AI Contact Center (AICC) case, leading to additional contracts and discussions on on-premise expansion. According to BizCrush, paid customers have increased each month since the initial paid payments were introduced in January 2026, and monthly revenue has grown more than threefold since full-scale billing started in March.

BizCrush launches its official commercial version ‘BizCrush Enterprise’ on August 31. The company submitted this product to the CES 2027 Innovation Awards in three categories: Artificial Intelligence, Software & Mobile Apps, and Accessibility, and plans to showcase it as a live working demo at the CES 2027 Eureka Park booth. Officials selected BizCrush for the Ministry of Science and ICT’s K-Tech Pioneers and Google’s Chang-Goo Program, and the company participated in San Francisco’s MARU Accelerator Program.

BizCrush CEO Taemin Kwak stated, “In quiet demonstration environments, performance differences between speech recognition services do not show clearly, but exhibition halls with constant background noise and dozens of languages passing through represent the actual usage environment itself.” He added, “With a structure where conversations at the booth become product demonstrations, showing actual environment performance as it is on the global stage of CES serves as the primary purpose of participation.” He continued, “Allowing anyone to verify performance claims directly on the open benchmark and presenting execution plans through concrete milestones with dates, we will build trust in global markets step by step.”

AVING News has promoted South Korean companies worldwide through media partnerships with more than 800 outlets in 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building upon its global media network, AVING News newly launched the ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ last August. Global US IT and tech media outlet Ubergizmo participated in this ‘Global Media Meetup’.
